title: End-of-life doula: vigil, planning, companionship, atmosphere, and nonmedical scope

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source perspective-axis synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no public rendering, no clinical/legal/operational/ritual authority.
limitations: Public sources support role vocabulary, authority boundaries, source limits, routing, and review needs only.
Perspective records must not be rendered as clinical, legal, emergency, funeral, investigative, ritual, therapeutic, or operational advice.
No role has total authority over a death. Every witness position sees and misses different things.
Public professional, official, or family-facing sources cannot replace consented witness testimony or community review.

moment.plain_scene: An end-of-life doula may hold vigil, help plan atmosphere, companionship, legacy, family conversation, and practical support, while remaining nonmedical and not replacing hospice, clinicians, social workers, chaplains, or tradition holders.

content_layers.observation_text: An end-of-life doula may hold vigil, help plan atmosphere, companionship, legacy, family conversation, and practical support, while remaining nonmedical and not replacing hospice, clinicians, social workers, chaplains, or tradition holders.
content_layers.source_synthesis: This record admits the witness role into the archive as evidence of position and limit. It does not grant the role total authority over meaning, timing, interior experience, legality, or what should be done.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: Rev0012 treats perspective as a first-class axis so records can say not only what happened, but who could see it, who could not, and what authority the account should not be given.

what_this_is_not: not a claim that this witness role is more truthful than all others
uncertainties: The current record is a source-bound scaffold, not a lived scene.
Role-specific testimony and review are needed before public rendering.
Institutional, cultural, legal, language, disability, class, race, geography, and family-structure factors may change what each role can witness.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface may say that different witnesses see different parts of dying. It must not use a role label to settle disputes, diagnose, determine time left, assign blame, or instruct next steps.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Practitioner surfaces should capture role, access, duration of contact, sensory channel, who was absent, what the witness could not know, and whether the account risks professional exposure or family identifiability.
language_notes: Name the witness role before generalizing from the account.
Separate observed facts from interpretation, memory, official category, and professional shorthand.
Do not collapse family memory, professional pattern recognition, official documentation, and first-person survivor account into one evidentiary type.
Protect vulnerable witnesses, children, workers, chosen-family members, and people with legal or employment exposure.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the perspective axis. Requires role-specific professional review, lived-witness testing, trauma review, and publication-language review before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is not medical advice. It does not diagnose, predict, verify death, recommend treatment, explain emergency action, or replace local care teams.
safety.legal_boundary: This record is not legal advice. Authority, documentation, custody, body release, investigation, family access, funeral, cremation, burial, benefits, and reporting rules are jurisdiction-specific.
